title: EIP-8360: TCREATE Opcode
description: Introduce a new opcode for creating contracts that exist only for the duration of a single transaction
author: Helkomine (@Helkomine), abc-123-c (@abc-123-c), Milos (@milonite), Peter Phillips (@PeterMPhillips)
bodyPreview: ## Abstract This EIP introduces a new EVM opcode, `TCREATE`, where `T` stands for transient, providing an official, gas-efficient, and state-aware mechanism for deploying temporary contracts. ## Motivation Many Ethereum applications do not require deployed code to persist beyond a single transaction. Examples include state-channel contracts, single-use accounts, and other ephemeral execution environments. Today, such patterns rely on a combination of `CREATE`/`CREATE2` and `SELFDESTRUCT`. However, `SELFDESTRUCT` has no longer provided gas refunds since [EIP-3529](./eip-3529.md), can only delete contracts created within the same transaction since the Cancun upgrade, and is expected to undergo further semantic restrictions in future protocol upgrades. As a result, the deploy-and-self-destruct pattern is no longer economically attractive, nor can its long-term behavior be relied upon. Providing a dedicated EVM opcode for temporary contract deployment offers a lower-cost alternative while improving state management by preventing unnecessary long-term code accumulation. This proposal also provides a gradual migration path away from `SELFDESTRUCT`. The proposal is fully compatible with account abstraction. Existing account semantics remain unchanged, while accounts may deploy transient contracts to implement extended execution logic entirely through calldata, for example, hook-based execution. Such hooks may execute dedicated logic or serve as reusable code templates that are invoked through `DELEGATECALL`. ## Specification ### Parameters | Parameter| Description| Value | Source | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `TCREATE` | New opcode | TBD | This EIP | | `BASE_OPCODE_COST` | Base opcode cost | 100 | This EIP | | `CPSB` | State gas price per byte | 1530 | [EIP-8037](./eip-8037.md) | | `STATE_BYTES_PER_NEW_ACCOUNT`| State bytes created per account| 120 | [EIP-8037](./eip-8037.md) | | `WARM_ACCESS` | Touch of an already warm account or storage slot| 100 | [EIP-8038](./eip-8038.md) | | `COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS` | Cold touch of an account | 3000 | [EIP-8038](./eip-8038.md) | | `ACCOUNT_WRITE` | Write to an account's leaf values (nonce, balance, code hash), charged per operation | 9000 | [EIP-8038](./eip-8038.md) | ### Semantics The behavior of `CREATE2` is defined in [EIP-1014](./eip-1014.md). `TCREATE` behaves identically to `CREATE2` except for the following changes: - The address is computed as `keccak256(0xfe || deployer_address || salt || keccak256(init_code))[12:]`, where `deployer_address` is the address of the account that executes `TCREATE` (the value returned by `ADDRESS` in the executing frame) and `||` denotes byte concatenation. - The nonce of the account at `deployer_address` is not incremented. This applies in every outcome, including an address collision and a `REVERT` or exceptional halt of the initcode. Nonce changes caused by the initcode follow their existing rules. The nonce limit of [EIP-2681](./eip-2681.md) still applies: if the nonce of the account at `deployer_address` is `2^64-1`, `TCREATE` ends with `0` pushed on the stack and the target address is not accessed, as for `CREATE2`. - At the end of the transaction, the code and nonce that the target account has during the transaction are discarded and are not written to the state. The account balance is preserved. An account that becomes empty is removed from the state at the end of the transaction in accordance with [EIP-161](./eip-161.md). The semantics are clarified further [here](#state-transition-handling). - Code deployment rules and collision semantics are identical to `CREATE2`, except for the nonce rule above and the gas rules in [Gas Accounting](#gas-accounting). If the target address has a nonzero nonce or a nonzero code length, the creation fails as specified in [EIP-684](./eip-684.md): the initcode is not executed, `0` is pushed on the stack, and the gas passed to the creation is consumed. The target account has a nonzero nonce from the start of its initcode execution until the end of the transaction, unless the creation fails, so a further `TCREATE` to the same address in that transaction fails in this way. ### State transition handling At the end of the transaction, the account state of every `TCREATE` account is finalized as follows: - The account nonce is 0. - The account has no code. - The account balance is preserved. A `TCREATE` account has no storage, because `SLOAD` and `SSTORE` halt in its context (see [`SLOAD` and `SSTORE` handling](#sload-and-sstore-handling)). Before the transaction, a `TCREATE` address has a zero nonce and no code, because otherwise the creation fails in accordance with [EIP-684](./eip-684.md). The post-transaction state of the account therefore differs from its pre-transaction state only in its balance, and finalization does not delete code or storage from the state. The only state entry that finalization can remove is an empty account, in accordance with [EIP-161](./eip-161.md). ### `TCREATE` accounts A *`TCREATE` account* is the account at an address computed by `TCREATE` in the current transaction. An address is a `TCREATE` account from the start of initcode execution at that address until the end of the transaction. If that `TCREATE` fails, or a frame that contains it reverts, the address is no longer a `TCREATE` account. Code executes *in the context of* a `TCREATE` account when the current address, as returned by `ADDRESS`, is a `TCREATE` account. This includes the initcode and the runtime code of that account, and code that the account executes through `DELEGATECALL` or `CALLCODE`. It does not include code that executes with another current address: code of accounts that the `TCREATE` account calls or creates with `CREATE`, and code of the `TCREATE` account that another account executes through `DELEGATECALL`, `CALLCODE`, or an [EIP-7702](./eip-7702.md) delegation.
